items.title: Parallax: Why AI Agents That Think Must Never Act
items.title_zh: Parallax：为何会思考的 AI 智能体绝不应直接行动
items.summary: Parallax argues prompt-level guardrails are architecturally insufficient for agents with execution capability and proposes cognitive-executive separation, adversarial validation with graduated determinism, information flow control and reversible execution. Its open-source Go reference implementation, OpenParallax, blocks 98.9% of 280 adversarial test cases with zero false positives under default configuration and 100% at maximum security, holding even when the reasoning system is assumed compromised.

items.title: SemiFA: An Agentic Multi-Modal Framework for Autonomous Semiconductor Failure Analysis Report Generation
items.title_zh: SemiFA：面向半导体失效分析报告自动生成的智能体多模态框架
items.summary: SemiFA is a four-agent LangGraph pipeline that generates structured semiconductor failure-analysis reports from inspection images in 48 seconds, combining DINOv2 and LLaVA-1.6 defect description with SECS/GEM telemetry fused with historically similar defects retrieved from a Qdrant vector database. Its DINOv2 classifier reaches 92.1% accuracy on 140 validation images, and a GPT-4o judge ablation found multimodal fusion improves root-cause reasoning by 0.86 composite points over an image-only baseline.

items.title: From Handwriting to Structured Data: Benchmarking AI Digitisation of Handwritten Forms
items.title_zh: 从手写到结构化数据：基准测试 AI 对手写表单的数字化
items.summary: The study benchmarks 17 frontier multimodal and open-source models on a challenging real-world medical handwritten form, finding the latest Google and OpenAI models reach accuracies around 85% with weighted F1 near 90% on discrete fields. GPT-5.4 had the lowest hallucination rate at 6%, Gemini 3.1 delivered the best overall performance, and prompt optimization raised macro precision, recall and F1 by over 60% while barely moving weighted metrics.

items.title: Concrete Jungle: Towards Concreteness Paved Contrastive Negative Mining for Compositional Understanding
items.title_zh: Concrete Jungle：以具体性铺就面向组合理解的对比负样本挖掘
items.summary: The paper establishes lexical concreteness as a determinant of negative-sample efficacy in contrastive pretraining, since modifying highly concrete terms yields stronger structural and visual discrepancies, and proposes ConcretePlant to isolate and manipulate perceptually grounded concepts. It identifies gradient imbalance in InfoNCE and introduces the margin-based Cement loss, with the integrated Slipform framework reaching state-of-the-art accuracy on compositional benchmarks, cross-modal retrieval and linear probing.

items.title: Indexing Multimodal Language Models for Large-scale Image Retrieval
items.title_zh: 面向大规模图像检索的多模态语言模型索引
items.summary: The work investigates multimodal LLMs as training-free similarity estimators for instance-level image-to-image retrieval, prompting the model with paired images and converting next-token probabilities into similarity scores for zero-shot re-ranking. Combined with memory-efficient indexing and top-k candidate re-ranking, MLLMs outperform task-specific re-rankers outside their native domains and are more robust to clutter, occlusion and small objects, though they fail under severe appearance changes.

items.title: Listening Alone, Understanding Together: Collaborative Context Recovery for Privacy-Aware AI
items.title_zh: 独自聆听，共同理解：面向隐私感知 AI 的协作式上下文恢复
items.summary: CONCORD is a privacy-aware asynchronous assistant-to-assistant framework that enforces owner-only speech capture via real-time speaker verification, then recovers missing context through spatio-temporal resolution, information-gap detection and minimal relationship-aware queries. Across a multi-domain dialogue dataset it achieves 91.4% recall in gap detection, 96% relationship classification accuracy and a 97% true negative rate in privacy-sensitive disclosure decisions.

items.title: One Token Away from Collapse: The Fragility of Instruction-Tuned Helpfulness
items.title_zh: 距崩溃仅一步之遥：指令微调有用性的脆弱性
items.summary: The study shows simple lexical constraints such as banning one punctuation character or common word cause instruction-tuned LLMs to lose 14-48% of comprehensiveness across seven models, with information criteria degrading 1.5-2.3 times more than surface criteria in blinded human evaluation. Diagnostics identify a planning failure: two-pass generation recovers 59-96% of response length, linear probes predict length with R^2 of 0.51-0.94, and pairwise evaluation reveals a 23% quality drop where independent LLM-as-judge sees only 3.5%.

items.title: Peer-Predictive Self-Training for Language Model Reasoning
items.title_zh: 面向语言模型推理的同伴预测自训练
items.summary: PST is a label-free fine-tuning framework in which multiple language models generate responses sequentially and the cross-model aggregate, often more reliable than individual answers, serves as an internal training signal weighted by pointwise mutual information. On math reasoning benchmarks it improves exact-match accuracy by 2.2-4.3 points across three small models and reduces the generator-verifier gap by 26-40% without external supervision.

items.title: When Less Latent Leads to Better Relay: Information-Preserving Compression for Latent Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
items.title_zh: 更少潜状态，更好中继：潜空间多智能体 LLM 协作的信息保留压缩
items.summary: The paper adapts KV-cache eviction to latent multi-agent LLM relays and proposes Orthogonal BackFill, which injects a low-rank residual from discarded KV states. Retaining 9.9%-20.2% of prompt KV cuts bandwidth by 4.7x and GPU memory by 8% while staying close to full relay across nine benchmarks.

items.title: AgentSPEX: An Agent SPecification and EXecution Language
items.summary: AgentSPEX is an agent specification and execution language for LLM-agent workflows with typed steps, branching, loops, parallel execution, reusable submodules and explicit state management, plus a custom harness and visual editor, evaluated on seven benchmarks.

items.title: Text-Attributed Knowledge Graph Enrichment with Large Language Models for Medical Concept Representation
items.title_zh: 用大语言模型丰富文本属性知识图谱，实现医学概念表示
items.summary: MedCo is an LLM-powered graph learning framework that builds a medical-code knowledge graph, enriches it into a text-attributed graph with generated node descriptions and edge rationales, and jointly trains a LoRA-tuned LLaMA encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network to improve medical concept representation.
